title: Remembering answers
summary: A cache keeps recent answers in memory so the database is asked less.

steps.title: The same question again
steps.text: Most people ask for the same few things: today's top stories, a popular profile. Asking the database each time repeats work. A cache keeps the last answer in fast memory and hands it back.

steps.prompt: The database is nearly full. Put a cache between the servers and the database.

between.note: A cache helps most between the servers and the database, so the servers ask it first. Drop it onto the line between them.

steps.hint: Drag Cache from the Data stores group onto the line from the servers to the database.

steps.title: Fresh versus fast
steps.text: A cache entry has a time to live (TTL), how long it is kept. A long TTL means more hits but older answers. A short TTL means fresher answers but more trips to the database.

steps.q: A cache answers 90 percent of questions. How much work reaches the database?
What is the cost of a long TTL?
choices: It costs more money to run
Answers may be out of date
steps.why: The cache can hand back something that has since changed.

choices: Written once and never read again
Private to one user each time
steps.why: Reused answers are where the savings are.

takeaway: A cache trades a little freshness for a lot of speed and a calmer database.
